structure: One ruling file, workareas/shared/design-release-2-1/sources/ruling-sam-2026-10-09-pm.md, about 706 lines (55 KB), scope the whole file. Lines 1-110 quote Sam verbatim, point by point from answers-2026-10-09-pm.md: search boxes (point 1), the prototype's JavaScript (point 3), ask-design rows (3a), live filtering and row lists (3b), commodities (2), documents (4), transporters (5), amend/cancel amendment/copy as new/delete (6), ownership of overview, check answers, declaration and confirmation (7), matching plants (7a), how plants changes are made (7b), the INS front door (8 and 8a) and the order of work (9). Lines 111-136 explain the orchestrator-versus-Sam marking, what ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers instead, the four evidence files and the design-question numbering. Lines 137-706 list 60 numbered claims in eleven lettered sections: (a) search boxes, claims 1-4; (b) the JavaScript rule, 5-7; (c) ask-design rows and design questions 1-13, 8-22; (d) rows built with GOV.UK or MoJ, 23-27; (e) commodities wait on MDM, 28-33; (f) transporter management waits, 34-37; (g) documents, 38; (h) ownership of overview/review/declaration/confirmation, 39-42; (i) plants changes in the same increment, 43-51; (j) the INS dashboard and the animals dashboard theme, 52-59; (k) ready against blocked, 60. Most claims are the orchestrator's application of Sam's principles and name backlog rows (inc-NNN), requirements (req-NNN) and conflicts (c-NNN). Nothing is left out of scope. Because the file is long and dense with row-by-row calls, it is cut into three parts on its lettered sections; every part reads the verbatim quote in full, because each listed claim is checked against it.
